title: Korčula Travel Guide: Beaches, Parking & Where to Stay
metaDescription: Plan your trip to Korčula, Croatia. Discover the best areas to stay, driving routes from Europe, ferry information, parking, and top beaches.
intro:
Korčula appeals to travelers seeking historical architecture, distinct local wine, and a quieter atmosphere than neighboring Hvar. The island features dense pine forests, rocky coastlines, and a fortified main town situated on a small peninsula. Visitors spend their time exploring narrow stone alleys, visiting family-run wineries in the interior, and swimming in pebble or rare sandy coves.

The main season runs from late spring to early autumn. Most driving visitors arrive via the car ferry from Orebić, which is reached by crossing the Pelješac Bridge, or by taking the longer car ferry from Split. The island accommodates both short stays focused on Korčula Town and longer holidays requiring a car to explore western settlements like Vela Luka.

areas.name: Korčula Town
areas.parking: Paid lots outside the pedestrian walls; high daily rates
areas.beach: 5-minute walk to Banje (pebble) or rocky spots
areas.summary: The historical and cultural center of the island. It offers the highest concentration of restaurants, museums, and boat tour departures.

areas.name: Lumbarda
areas.bestFor: Families with children and wine lovers
areas.parking: Generally free or inexpensive street parking
areas.beach: Direct access to Vela Pržina and Bilin Žal (sandy)
areas.summary: A relaxed village located 6 kilometers from Korčula Town. It is famous for Grk wine production and the island's only natural sandy beaches.

areas.name: Vela Luka
areas.bestFor: Travelers seeking a quieter, more local environment
areas.parking: Plentiful and mostly free around accommodations
areas.beach: Short boat ride to Proizd island (clear pebble/rock)
areas.summary: The largest town on the island, situated on the western end. It serves as the main port for car ferries arriving directly from Split.

areas.name: Žrnovo & Interior Villages
areas.bestFor: Hikers, foodies, and those looking for seclusion
areas.parking: Easy and free at most guesthouses
areas.beach: 10-15 minute drive to south coast pebble coves
areas.summary: A cluster of small, traditional hamlets set back from the sea. The area is known for agrotourism, traditional macaroni dishes, and forested hiking trails.

whenToGo: June and September offer sea temperatures around 23-25°C, mild weather, and full service without peak crowds. July and August bring peak heat, 26°C waters, highest accommodation prices, and busy ferries. October and May see cooling waters (19-21°C), reduced ferry schedules, and many seasonal restaurants closing, making these months better for hiking and historical sightseeing than swimming.

faq.question: Is Korčula worth visiting?
faq.answer: Yes, for its well-preserved medieval town, distinct wine culture, and clear coastal waters. It offers a quieter, more historical alternative to the party atmosphere of neighboring islands.

faq.question: How many days do you need in Korčula?
faq.answer: Three to four days is optimal for a visit. This provides enough time to see Korčula Town, visit Lumbarda's vineyards, and drive to a few southern pebble beaches.

faq.question: What is the best beach in Korčula?
faq.answer: Vela Pržina and Bilin Žal in Lumbarda are the best sandy beaches, making them popular for families. Pupnatska Luka on the south coast is widely considered the top pebble beach for its clear water and forested backdrop.

faq.question: Do I need a car in Korčula?
faq.answer: A car is not needed if you only plan to stay in Korčula Town and take boat tours. However, a vehicle is highly recommended for exploring the island's hidden coves, interior vineyards, and western towns.

faq.question: Where can I park in Korčula Town?
faq.answer: Korčula Town has paid parking lots outside the pedestrian zone, such as the eastern port lot or near the Tommy supermarket. Smaller towns and villages across the island typically offer free or cheaper street parking.

faq.question: Is Korčula good for families?
faq.answer: Yes, the island is very safe and features several family-friendly areas. Lumbarda is particularly popular for families due to its shallow sandy beaches and relaxed, walkable environment.
